summary: iter353 review — PIN hashing + admin-managed CORS allowlist. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter353_pin_hashing_and_cors.py: 34/36 passed. All security-critical guarantees hold: (a) zero plaintext `pin`/`guest_pin` documents in Mongo (users, members, users.guest_pin all 0); (b) test member's pin_lookup == HMAC-SHA256(pepper, '4321') and is NOT the naked sha256 of '4321', so the pepper is applied; (c) PUT /api/members/{id} and PUT /api/admin/users/{id} both store only pin_lookup and no plaintext; (d) GET /api/members/{id} and /api/members list correctly strip pin/pin_lookup and expose pin_set:true; (e) kiosk pin-checkin lookup + wrong-PIN 404, staff /api/checkins/pin + wrong-PIN 404, kiosk unlock 8712 (admin@5812global.org owns it) + wrong-PIN 401 with uniform 'Invalid credentials', qr-scan with PIN resolves; (f) visitor-register returns a pin in the body and persists ONLY guest_pin_lookup + pin_lookup digests, no plaintext; (g) supervisor override's pin_query() resolves the privileged user by digest, wrong digest resolves nobody; (h) all 7 seeded CORS origins present, invalid values (wildcard, non-domain, non-list) 400 with helpful message, bare host normalised to https://, duplicates collapsed, non-admin can't PUT; (i) OPTIONS preflights hit at http://localhost:8001 correctly echo ACAO for app.lubwamas.org and the built-in preview.emergentagent.com regex, and return no ACAO for evil.example.com; (j) a newly-added CORS origin goes live and becomes ACAO-allowed within ~60s WITHOUT a backend restart. Frontend Allowed Web Domains editor at /admin → Security is fully functional: 7 chips render, adding portal.lubwamas.org normalises to https:// and persists across reload, removing via cors-remove-<origin> works, and 'https://*.bad.com/x' surfaces the backend 400 as a toast ("'https://*.bad.com/x' is not a valid origin — use the form https://app.example.org (no path, no wildcard)") without adding the entry. MemberForm.jsx source verified: pin field is empty on load, shows 'Set' badge when data.pin_set is true, placeholder reads 'Leave blank to keep current PIN', helper text says 'Stored encrypted — it can't be read back, only replaced.' (Note: current /people page in this build only surfaces Guests & Parents / Families / Children / Family Approvals tabs, so the members-editor could not be exercised end-to-end in the browser — code review passes.)

critical.issue: Directory endpoint leaks the pin_lookup digest in the response body — should strip pin_lookup and return pin_set:bool (as /api/admin/users/{id}/profile already does). Currently only password_hash is projected out; pin_lookup is visible to any admin caller. Fix: mirror the pop-and-set-pin_set logic from get_user_full_profile.

Sending {clear_pin: true} does NOT clear the member's PIN — the MemberUpdate Pydantic model (backend/models.py:57) has no `clear_pin` field, so it is stripped before apply_pin_fields runs. Test PIN 4321 still resolves via kiosk pin-checkin after clear_pin. Add `clear_pin: Optional[bool] = None` to MemberUpdate (and let apply_pin_fields handle it). This is the exact semantic the review request calls out.

minor.issue: Sending ONLY {"pin": ""} (no other field) returns 400 'No valid fields to update' because `pin` is not in ACCOUNT_FIELDS and apply_pin_fields returns an empty update. This is arguably correct — the frontend always sends other fields — but the review request's literal case ({pin:''} alone) does not succeed. Frontend behaviour unaffected. Optional: treat a pin-only payload as a no-op 200.

integration_issues.issue: Current UnifiedPeoplePage in this deployment only surfaces Guests & Parents / Families / Children / Family Approvals tabs — the members editor (which owns member-pin-input / member-pin-set-badge) is not reachable from the /people UI in the browser. Code inspection of MemberForm.jsx confirms all data-testids and the write-only behaviour are wired correctly; /members route redirects back to /people.

action_items: Strip pin_lookup from GET /api/admin/users/{id} response and expose pin_set:bool instead (parity with /users/{id}/profile).
Add `clear_pin: Optional[bool] = None` to MemberUpdate in backend/models.py so PUT /api/members/{id} with {clear_pin:true} actually removes the PIN.
Optional polish: surface member editor in the /people UI so admins can exercise the write-only PIN field.
critical_code_review_comments: pin_security.py cleanly separates the pepper into env and only stores keyed digests — good.
The DynamicCORSMiddleware+refresh loop is minimal (only is_allowed_origin overridden) — nice. 60s propagation is a good trade-off.
backend/routers/admin.py get_user endpoint at ~line 280 needs the same PIN-strip that get_user_full_profile applies at lines 299-303 — this is a straight-forward parity fix.
MemberUpdate is missing clear_pin — Pydantic silently drops unknown keys before apply_pin_fields sees them, so the admin.py-style clear_pin escape hatch doesn't work for members.

Visitor-register writes both guest_pin_lookup and pin_lookup on the user, but no member row gets pin_lookup — so the returned PIN doesn't actually resolve at /api/kiosk/pin-checkin (queries members) or /api/kiosk/unlock (requires privileged role). Consider seeding member.pin_lookup on visitor-register so the kiosk lookup path works end-to-end.

success_rate.frontend: CORS manager 100% (7 chips, add/persist-through-reload/remove/invalid-toast all pass); MemberForm reachability blocked by /people UI tabs (code review passes)

rca of the issue: Bug 1 (admin/users/{id} leak): backend/routers/admin.py:280 uses only {"_id":0,"password_hash":0} projection; the newer PIN scheme forgot to also strip pin_lookup here (the /profile variant at line 285 was updated correctly).
